figmaExecutionNotes: Use light theme with warm collaboration accents; do not use a white hero background.
Hero headline should be set smaller because the word count is 17; keep copy exact.
Trust section must prioritize logos/social proof over badges.
Feature sections should use consistent 4-card grids with tight vertical rhythm and no large empty areas.
Avoid strip-like layouts unless required by the trust/logos row; do not overuse thin horizontal banners.
Keep desktop and mobile parity in content; on mobile stack hero text below visual and convert feature grids to single-column cards.
Do not invent unsupported sections such as pricing, testimonials, forms, or news.

accentVisuals: floating trust chip: Trusted by 100,000+ Businesses Globally
heroStrategy.headline: Elevate Your Team’s Productivity with Zoho Workplace
heroStrategy.subheadline: A Complete Email & Collaboration Suite for Enterprises that Facilitates Unified Communication.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use a right-aligned enterprise message block with a left-side layered product scene: a realistic Zoho Workplace dashboard mockup, stacked communication chips, and a compact trust strip. Keep the hero visually dense and premium, with red accent CTAs, white surfaces, soft shadows, and subtle grid-line decor. The product story should feel controlled and high-trust, not promotional. Pair this with alternating feature sections below, including at least one dark section for contrast and one more decorative section with orbs/mesh elements.

repetitionBreakers: Hero uses split-left-image-right-text with floating proof chips for dynamic continuity
Trust section uses a static logo grid directly after the hero instead of a generic metrics band
Product area alternates between spotlight-plus-grid and accordion-with-visual to avoid repeated card grids
Testimonials use a spotlighted single-quote layout rather than a uniform grid
Pricing is treated as a highlighted cart card to create a decisive closing contrast
blueprint.pageTitle: Zoho Workplace for Enterprises | Unified Email & Collaboration Suite
blueprint.metaDescription: Explore Zoho Workplace, a unified email and collaboration suite for enterprises. See how teams communicate, collaborate, and work securely from anywhere with one platform.

sections.backgroundTreatment: clean white base with subtle grid-line texture, framed workspace mockup, and floating proof chips
sections.designNote: Use a content-first split hero that answers what it is, who it is for, and what to do next. Left side: headline, subheadline, support line, and a solid red Get started CTA. Right side: realistic Zoho Workplace UI composite with Mail, Cliq, Writer, Meeting, and Connect chips. Add a compact trust row under the CTA so the ad-to-landing continuity stays strong for warm traffic.

Place trust immediately after the hero using 3-6 recognizable customer logos in a clean static grid. Keep it high-contrast but restrained, with a short trust caption above the logos. Do not use a marquee. If usable logos are unavailable, fall back to a single metric strip with the 100,000+ businesses claim.

Consolidate the long feature content into two expressive product blocks rather than a generic SaaS grid. First block: spotlight-plus-grid focused on the click-driving benefits, especially all-in-one workspace and real-time collaboration, with a preview panel showing app switching reduction. Second block: accordion-with-visual for integrations, security, and workflow control to handle the larger content volume without flattening the page. Keep alternating backgrounds and visual weight so each block feels distinct.

Since there is no why-Techjockey content, omit this as a standalone persuasion section and repurpose the slot into a compact decision-support strip inside the product area if needed. If the section must render, keep it as a minimal icon-list with seller-assist value only, avoiding any generic agency-style pitch.

Convert the pricing area into a purchase-ready highlighted card rather than a comparison table. Present the included enterprise plan items as a dense checklist with the red Get started CTA. Keep the card visually prominent, but not oversized, so it feels like a natural decision point after proof and features.

Use a single spotlight testimonial followed by a small supporting set of quotes, not a repetitive uniform grid. Since there are 5 testimonials, make the first one larger and allow the rest to sit in a controlled carousel or stacked quote rail. Keep the emphasis on operational clarity, productivity, and seamless collaboration.

End with a strong conversion card that repeats only the single allowed CTA label, Get started. Keep the form or purchase prompt concise, use a full-width mobile CTA, and visually separate it from the testimonials with generous spacing and a clean framed surface.

Do not use a moving marquee. If this slot is retained, make it a quiet static logo strip or omit it entirely because the main proof requirement is already satisfied earlier. This section should never compete with the primary CTA path.

blueprint.designPersonality: Confident, organized, and enterprise-practical with a clean marketplace finish. The page should feel like a trusted software buying destination: logo-led, crisp, efficient, and premium without being flashy.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use a layered enterprise workspace composition: a realistic Zoho Workplace dashboard mockup, adjacent floating communication chips (Mail, Cliq, Writer, Meeting, Connect), and a prominent trust strip with customer logos directly beneath the hero. Keep image proportions balanced so no section feels sparse; pair every feature block with a dense supporting visual, metric tile, or app stack illustration.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Single-column top banner with brand logo, large headline, short supporting copy, and a compact benefit list; no split media treatment visible in the reference HTML.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Hero banner → lead form card directly below; content follows a conversion-first stack with minimal intermediate marketing sections in the provided markup.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Simple rectangular form card with clear header, stacked fields, and utilitarian presentation; no glass, shadow-heavy, or hover-driven card system evident.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary conversion CTA embedded in the hero/form flow; emphasis on one dominant action, with supporting lead capture rather than multiple competing CTAs.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No pricing module detected in the reference HTML.
referenceMap.footerMode: Footer not present in the provided markup.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Logo-only branding in hero; no visible product imagery, media panel, or illustration-based storytelling in the extracted HTML.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Content map suggests feature-led sections with repeated headline + description + 4-up feature lists; structurally best represented as stacked informational blocks rather than tabs or accordions.
referenceMap.formPattern: Lead-capture form card with hidden tracking fields and a visible field stack; conversion-oriented and likely positioned immediately after the hero.
referenceMap.animationStyle: Static, non-animated presentation inferred from markup; no motion system exposed in the HTML.
designNotes: Use a conversion-first layout with the hero immediately followed by a form module.
Keep hierarchy strict: logo, headline, short proof/benefits, then capture form.
Favor compact lists over dense paragraphs for value communication.
Reserve dark or high-contrast bands for top-level emphasis and trust cues.
Design feature sections as repeating modular blocks for scalable long-form pages.
No evidence of advanced interaction patterns such as carousels, tabs, accordions, or sticky CTAs in the reference HTML.

mustHaveMoments: Prominent trust strip immediately after hero with logo-led proof and the 100,000+ businesses message
Clear hero message paired with a strong primary CTA and free trial cue
Feature blocks that are tightly spaced and content-accurate, with no oversized empty gaps
Dedicated pricing/cart section with complete plan inclusions and Get Started CTA
Integration showcase with recognizable app categories to reinforce ecosystem value
Testimonial section with concise enterprise-focused quotes to reduce purchase hesitation
avoidPatterns: Do not use strip-heavy layouts repeatedly across the page
Do not leave large empty spaces beside features or media blocks
Do not misalign images or place small visuals against large unused areas
Do not omit the cart/pricing section
Do not deviate from the provided content copy or hero messaging
Do not rely on generic decorative visuals instead of proof and product clarity
designStrategy.reasoning: Zoho Workplace is a solution-aware enterprise collaboration suite, so the page should convert by proving credibility, clarity, and business value quickly. Since visitors trust logos most, the dominant trust signal should be a logo-first proof moment early in the page, supported by the 100,000+ businesses claim. The content is long and feature-rich, so the layout should be dense and structured rather than airy, ensuring every section earns attention without wasted space. A split hero works best because it can pair the value proposition with a strong CTA and a product/proof visual treatment. The overall tone should feel efficient and enterprise-safe, with strong CTA intent because the page goal is lead generation via free trial or get started action.
